subject: HealthSync RFI: cross-border transfer evidence, DPA annex and DPF items
messages:
From: Kaitlyn Morris <kaitlyn.morris@healthsync.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>; procurement@healthsync.com
Cc: legal@healthsync.com
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthSync RFI — cross-border transfers and DPA annex follow-up

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our security and privacy review we need a bit more detail to close on the contract: a consolidated data protection framework (DPF) mapping for EU→US transfers, the proposed DPA annex with any delegation/subprocessor language, and evidence of technical controls (encryption in transit and at rest, HSM/KMS usage). I attached our RFI tracker for line-item mapping.

Specifically we need:
- Mapping of data flows (EU data → Redwood hosted inference / Dedicated / Private) and legal basis for each leg.
- Confirmation of whether SCCs or DPF mechanism will be relied on for EU exports and any plan for UK transfers.
- Recent SOC 2 Type II report summary or controls snapshot.
- Current subprocessor list and notification cadence.
- Any support for data residency or VPC/private deployment options.

Can you provide a combined response with attachments by 2026-07-15? If you prefer, please send an initial package and we will mark open items in the tracker.

Attachment: healthsync_rfi_tracker.xlsx

Best,
Kaitlyn
Privacy Lead, HealthSync

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Kaitlyn Morris <kaitlyn.morris@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSync RFI — cross-border transfers and DPA annex follow-up

Kaitlyn — thank you, will do. Looping Marissa (account lead) and Neha (privacy/compliance) to coordinate.

Plan: Neha will draft the DPF mapping and a DPA annex template; Marissa and I will cover commercial/hosting options and residency notes. We should be able to share an initial package and controls snapshot within 10 business days.

Two quick clarifying Qs:
1) Do you want the DPF mapping to include inference caching/KV cache behaviors (we can include an operational note)?
2) For UK transfers, is there a requirement to rely on UK Addendum + SCCs or would a combination with technical mitigations be acceptable for now?

I’ll follow up with a proposed delivery plan.

Thanks,
Connor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-06T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL — Draft DPF mapping + evidence package (for review)

Connor / Marissa — attaching my draft bundle for review before we send to HealthSync. Highlights: I mapped three distinct flows (1. EU customer data sent to Redwood Hosted API; 2. EU data to Dedicated (regional) nodes; 3. On-prem/Private deployment option where customer controls keys).

Key notes:
- Legal basis: standard contract + SCCs for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private deployments we recommend controller-to-controller language and explicit customer-managed KMS.
- Technical controls: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest (disk), envelope encryption with KMS/HSM for key wrapping. We call out tokenization of PII at request edge as an implementation pattern.
- KV cache: ephemeral, not persisted to durable storage for Hosted; Dedicated supports configurable KV persistence per tenant.
- Subprocessors: included current list and next review cadence (quarterly).

Attachments I prepared: redwood_dpf_controls_snapshot.pdf, SOC2-TypeII-evidence-summary.pdf, dpa_annex_draft_healthsync_v1.docx

Open items where I need HealthSync confirmation:
- Whether they require SCCs + UK Addendum or want us to propose a DPF-transfer mapping supported by contractual guarantees and additional technical measures.
- If they expect a single-sign-off on subprocessor changes or pre-approval for specific categories.

Please review and flag anything to soften before we send externally. I’ve kept the DPA annex template conservative on subprocessors.

— Neha
Privacy & Compliance

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Kaitlyn Morris <kaitlyn.morris@healthsync.com>; procurement@healthsync.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, legal@healthsync.com
Date: 2026-07-10T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSync RFI — cross-border transfers and DPA annex follow-up

Kaitlyn — thanks for the clear list. Please find our consolidated package attached and a short summary below. We can set a call next week to walk through any line items in the tracker.

Package attached: redwood_dpf_controls_snapshot.pdf; dpa_annex_draft_healthsync_v1.docx; SOC2-TypeII-evidence-summary.pdf

Summary:
- Transfers/legal basis: For Hosted and Dedicated offerings we propose SCCs (EU + UK Addendum where applicable) as the primary transfer mechanism; we will execute an appropriate DPA annex. For customers who require controller-to-controller separation we offer the Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed keys.
- Technical controls: TLS 1.3, AES-256 at rest, envelope encryption w/ KMS/HSM, optional field-level tokenization. Ephemeral KV cache for Hosted; optional persistent KV on Dedicated only if enabled in tenant config.
- Subprocessors: current list and date of onboarding included in the controls snapshot; we notify customers 30 days prior to material changes and provide the option for additional review for enterprise contracts.

Open items we would like confirmation on:
- HealthSync preference on SCCs + UK Addendum vs. an explicit DPF mechanism approach (we can produce a mapped statement aligned to their tracker).
- Whether you need a single pre-approval threshold for subprocessors or a category-based approval workflow.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_dpf_controls_snapshot.pdf] [Attachment: dpa_annex_draft_healthsync_v1.docx] [Attachment: SOC2-TypeII-evidence-summary.pdf]

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-dpf-package

If it helps, Marissa and I can coordinate a short 30-minute review with your privacy and procurement teams next Tue/Wed.

Regards,
Connor
Redwood Inference

From: Kaitlyn Morris <kaitlyn.morris@healthsync.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com, legal@healthsync.com
Date: 2026-07-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthSync RFI — cross-border transfers and DPA annex follow-up

Connor / team — thanks for the fast turnaround and the package. I reviewed the DPA annex and redwood_dpf_controls_snapshot.pdf. A couple of small asks before we move to legal review: we’ve uploaded a redline to your DPA annex (attached) with two edits: (1) a requested 45-day notification for subprocessor changes instead of 30, and (2) a minor change to section 5.2 (data retention carve-out for aggregated analytics).

We also need a short appendix that explicitly maps the inference cache behavior to the data categories in our tracker (PII / pseudonymized / aggregate). If you can send that last piece and accept the subprocessor notification 45-day window we can proceed to internal legal review and aim for a signature in the next 2–3 weeks.

Attachment: dpa_redline_healthsync.docx

Appreciate the help — Kaitlyn
Privacy Lead, HealthSync
